title: Selective Claim Analysis result v0.1 (source-grounded)
description: Compact downstream Claim Analysis view for the selective PoC lane. Its authority is SOURCE-GROUNDED EXTRACTION: every fact here is read from a case document and carries that document's exact quote and character range. It is NOT a projection of the canonical medical variables and must not be presented as one -- the PoC does not resolve field ids to canonical variable ids, so claiming projection authority would assert a binding that was never computed. medical_projection_status records that plainly. Conflict candidates stay candidates: consistency_check verifies them before any P6 ledger entry exists. Reading trace and performance telemetry live in claim_analysis_trace.json.

medical_projection_status.description: Whether a canonical medical projection governs this result. Pinned to not_configured for v0.1: config/medical/medical_projection_v0.1.json ships projection_enabled false with no field rules, so no field-to-variable mapping exists to project through. A constant rather than an enum because no other value is reachable in this version -- an enum would advertise a state the lane cannot occupy.

medical_revision_context.description: OPTIONAL, and context only. When a canonical medical revision happens to exist for the case, a result may record which one was current while it ran. It is not the source of any value here and never confers canonical authority; omit it entirely rather than record a revision this result did not actually observe. Declaring it is what makes the DAO verify the digest.

upstream_policy_snapshot.description: The policy-layer snapshot this artifact was derived from (Part 11I). Required whenever the artifact carries at least one policy reference: a downstream result is an assertion about what the policy layer said when it was written, so it records which bytes it read. The DAO recomputes this at write time and refuses a mismatch; `dao.py policy-snapshot` prints the current value. Per-document digests cover the normalized contract, boundary inventory, reference tables, processed source text, manifest entry (page_map included) and governing parent coverage -- the same set the document's audit binds to.

medical_revision_context.$comment: Inlined rather than $ref'd to medical_common.schema.json#/$defs/medical_variable_revision on purpose. Pointing at the canonical definition would re-import canonical medical vocabulary into a contract that explicitly does not claim canonical authority, and would couple this lane to a schema it must not modify.

value_state.description: What this single reading established. 'asserted' -- the source states a value. 'explicitly_absent' -- the source states the thing is NOT present (e.g. no acute fracture), which is a positive finding and needs its own quote. 'unavailable' -- nothing could be established. 'not_applicable' -- the case's own facts exclude the field. Silence is 'unavailable', never 'explicitly_absent': a document that says nothing has not denied anything.

partial_reading.description: True when this reading cited a real value that did NOT meet the four trusted-value requirements in extraction_policy.trusted_value_requirements -- it is complete: false, unambiguous: false, or both. Such a reading is recorded but never becomes canonical: it is never placed in selected_observation_ids, and the field it belongs to stays 'unavailable' unless some other source asserts a trusted value. It exists because the alternative was discarding the reading outright, which left the field reporting that no source mentioned it while the model had quoted the value verbatim -- measured on CASE_7015 (2026-08-26) as 5 of 40 unavailable fields, among them 사고일, 수술명 and 장해 영구성. Absent means an ordinary reading, so a producer that does not set it is unchanged.

complete.description: The model's own verdict that this reading captured the WHOLE value. False when the source states more than the reading carries -- a second 수술명 on the next line, a date given only as 3/26. Recorded only alongside partial_reading so a reviewer can tell which of the two requirements failed.

unambiguous.description: The model's own verdict that the text supports exactly one reading. False when the same passage could be read more than one way. Recorded only alongside partial_reading.

unavailable_reason.description: WHY a field has no value. Three of these are distinct records-management situations that a single value used to collapse -- measured on CASE_700 (2026-08-21), where all 25 unavailable fields read `not_mentioned` while the free-text reason held three different causes. `not_mentioned` means sources WERE read and none discussed the field, which is a real records gap a reviewer may close by requesting documents. `route_not_activated` means a conditional route never opened -- its trigger did not fire (산재 filing unconfirmed), so nothing was read and no document is missing; requesting records would be wasted effort. `not_scheduled` means an opportunistic field was never scheduled a read of its own: it answers only from documents another field already opened. `outside_poc_scope` means the pipeline has no producer for this source at all. Collapsing these into `not_mentioned` sends a reviewer looking for records that would not have helped, and hides that a route silently never ran. `partial_reading_only` means a priority source DID cite a value but it failed the trusted-value requirements (complete/unambiguous), so nothing became canonical -- the records are NOT silent and the quote is preserved in observations, so a reviewer should read the source rather than request more documents. It pairs with stop_reason partial_value_only (added 2026-08-26 after CASE_7015 showed such readings being discarded and reported as not_mentioned).

source_document_type.description: owner: claim analysis (stage 3-a). The COARSE type of a non-medical source, for an observation the type-conditional round read from a document that has no medical kind -- a 법률의견서, an insurer letter. Set INSTEAD of `source_document_kind`, never alongside it: the two name different axes, and defaulting a legal opinion to `other_medical` (as the retired industrial branch did) would label a lawyer's letter a medical record. An observation carrying this is by construction from stage 3-a.

source_priority_rank.description: The rung of the field's OWN route ladder this source sits on -- not the order the document happened to be opened in. An opportunistic reading records the rank its route assigns, so a value picked up from an already-open document is never mistaken for a higher-priority one.

extraction_wave.description: Which pass produced the observation. `type_conditional` is stage 3-a, the round that runs AFTER case-type assessment and re-opens fields the common A/B pass left unavailable; it is not a third wave of the common pass and never runs before a verdict exists.

extraction_method.description: How this reading was produced. 'deterministic_label_anchor' means a rule in claim_analysis_deterministic.py matched a label the FORM PUBLISHER prints (노동능력상실율(%), 수술명, the 임상적추정/최종진단 checkbox) and read the value beside it -- no model call was involved for this field, so the reading is exactly repeatable. 'model_read' is an ordinary provider extraction. Recorded because the two have different failure modes and a reviewer auditing a value needs to know which one produced it: a rule cannot hallucinate but can miss a variant form, while a model reads any phrasing but was measured returning different answers on the same text across runs (CASE_705 vs CASE_713, the observation that motivated the rule layer). Absent means model_read -- older contracts predate this axis.

rule_version.description: The rule set that produced a deterministic_label_anchor reading (e.g. claim_analysis_deterministic.v0.1). Present only with that extraction_method, so a value can be traced to the exact pattern version that read it when a pattern is later widened.

oneOf.$comment: asserted: a value, its source, and an exact quote.

allOf.$comment: Exactly one source axis. A medical form names `source_document_kind`; a non-medical document read by the type-conditional round names `source_document_type` instead. Requiring one of the two (rather than the medical one outright) is what lets stage 3-a cite a 법률의견서 without mislabelling it a medical record; forbidding both together is what stops a document being described on two axes at once.

oneOf.$comment: explicitly_absent: no value, but the sentence asserting absence is quoted. Its scope is this field only -- an absence statement about one finding never travels to another field.

allOf.$comment: Exactly one source axis. A medical form names `source_document_kind`; a non-medical document read by the type-conditional round names `source_document_type` instead. Requiring one of the two (rather than the medical one outright) is what lets stage 3-a cite a 법률의견서 without mislabelling it a medical record; forbidding both together is what stops a document being described on two axes at once.

oneOf.$comment: unavailable: nothing established, so there is nothing to cite.
not_applicable: excluded by the case's own facts, and the fact doing the excluding is quoted. Silence alone can never reach this state.

authority.description: Where this field's content came from. 'source_document_extraction' -- read from a case document with an exact citation. 'claim_analysis_native' -- a claim-side finding this stage owns (accident circumstances, filing information, case-type triggers), reserved for the event_timeline domain. 'legal_opinion_assertion' -- a judgement a party's counsel reached, read from a 법률의견서 with an exact citation. It is separated from `source_document_extraction` because two opposing opinions on one question are NOT a records contradiction to reconcile -- they are the dispute the case is about. Measured on CASE_053: DOC_006 (claimant) concluded 배상책임 성립 under 민법 제758조 and DOC_008 (insurer) concluded 불성립 on the same facts. Filing that as a conflict would ask a reviewer to pick a winner the records cannot settle; publishing both as opinions states the case accurately.

resolution_status.description: The field's settled state after its read ladder ran. Mirrors the observation vocabulary, plus 'conflict' for two sources that assert different values.

selected_observation_ids.description: The observation carrying the value this field reports. Exactly one when asserted; empty in every other state -- notably under conflict, where electing one reading would be choosing a winner this stage has no standing to choose.

stop_reason.description: Why this field's read ladder stopped. 'partial_value_only' -- every cited reading failed the trusted-value requirements (complete/unambiguous), so no value became canonical even though the sources were NOT silent. It is distinct from 'sources_exhausted', which means the ladder found nothing at all; conflating the two made a quoted-but-partial value indistinguishable from an absent one.

unavailable_reason.description: WHY a field has no value. Three of these are distinct records-management situations that a single value used to collapse -- measured on CASE_700 (2026-08-21), where all 25 unavailable fields read `not_mentioned` while the free-text reason held three different causes. `not_mentioned` means sources WERE read and none discussed the field, which is a real records gap a reviewer may close by requesting documents. `route_not_activated` means a conditional route never opened -- its trigger did not fire (산재 filing unconfirmed), so nothing was read and no document is missing; requesting records would be wasted effort. `not_scheduled` means an opportunistic field was never scheduled a read of its own: it answers only from documents another field already opened. `outside_poc_scope` means the pipeline has no producer for this source at all. Collapsing these into `not_mentioned` sends a reviewer looking for records that would not have helped, and hides that a route silently never ran. `partial_reading_only` means a priority source DID cite a value but it failed the trusted-value requirements (complete/unambiguous), so nothing became canonical -- the records are NOT silent and the quote is preserved in observations, so a reviewer should read the source rather than request more documents. It pairs with stop_reason partial_value_only (added 2026-08-26 after CASE_7015 showed such readings being discarded and reported as not_mentioned).

allOf.$comment: asserted: exactly one selected observation, and an asserted reading exists to be selected.
explicitly_absent: a grounded absence reading, and no selected value.

unavailable: nothing became canonical, and the reason why is named. Two shapes reach it and the difference is what a reviewer is owed. sources_exhausted -- no evidence anywhere, so every observation must itself be 'unavailable'. partial_value_only -- a priority source DID cite a value that failed the trusted-value requirements (complete/unambiguous), so the observations are 'asserted' and flagged partial_reading; the field still selects nothing and still asserts no value. Before partial_value_only existed such a reading was discarded and the field reported that no source mentioned it, contradicting a quote the model had reproduced verbatim (CASE_7015, 2026-08-26).

stop_reason.$comment: Expressed as an exclusion, NOT as an enum of the two allowed values. `test_stop_reason_enums_agree.py` scans every `stop_reason` node carrying an `enum` and requires them all to hold the full shared vocabulary -- a conditional listing a SUBSET reads to that guard as a schema that lost values, and it would also displace the result schema's real declaration from the position the guard samples. Saying which reasons an `unavailable` field may NOT carry keeps the restriction while leaving exactly one place that declares the vocabulary.

allOf.$comment: No evidence at all: every observation must itself be unavailable. Unchanged from before partial_value_only was added.

A partial reading is real cited evidence, so it must carry the partial_reading flag and at least one of complete/unambiguous must be false -- otherwise it would have met the trusted-value bar and should not be here. At least one such observation must exist, or the field had no partial reading to report.
not_applicable: at least one grounded observation carrying the excluding fact. Never reachable from silence -- that is what minItems plus the per-item evidence floor buys.
conflict: both readings kept, neither elected.

status.description: Whether this case type is in scope for review, judged independently of the other three. 'applicable' -- an extracted fact affirmatively triggers it. 'not_applicable' -- ONLY where a source affirmatively states the negative. 'uncertain' -- everything else, including silence. Silence is never not_applicable: a record that does not mention a vehicle has not established that no vehicle was involved. Scoped to the selective lane; legacy case_type_result keeps its own supported/not_supported vocabulary.

allOf.$comment: applicable needs a named trigger field and a quote -- the verdict must point at what produced it.
not_applicable requires affirmative negative evidence. Without this floor, silence could be filed as a decided verdict -- the exact failure the parallel judgment exists to prevent.

clause_ref.description: The specific clause text stating this requirement, when one was located. Verified by the DAO on the same terms as the coverage-level clause_ref: canonical UID state, policy-stage-passed, and snapshot freshness.
